papers_read.title_as_printed: Pack file pdf/P-114.txt is the San-Martin et al. EEG/LORETA paper (BSPC 66 (2021) 102499), P-112's paper. The paper the record means (claim '93% Acc', registry row Kinect/ANFIS gait, summaries.md header 1-s2.0-S1746809421003195) is Seifallahi et al., 'Detection of mild cognitive Impairment from gait using Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference system', BSPC 71 (2022) 103195, present in the pack as pdf/P-115.txt. Both read in full; verdict uses the gait paper.
Machine learning approaches to mild cognitive impairment detection based on structural MRI data and morphometric features (Zubrikhina et al., Cognitive Systems Research 78 (2023) 87-95)

what_each_reports.P-114: Kinect V2 dual-task gait features, 150 older adults (70 MCI, 80 HC, IDAA Tehran), hierarchical ANFIS binary MCI vs HC accuracy 93% (sens 90%, spec 99%, F-score 91.5%); LR 81.25% and SVM 78.85% on the same features. ANFIS evaluation protocol not stated.
what_each_reports.P-99: 207 participants (145 MCI, 62 HC; Moscow Mental-health clinic No. 1 / Memory Clinic), FreeSurfer morphometric features from T1 MRI, chi-squared SelectKBest plus six classifiers, 10-fold CV. Best: SVC accuracy 0.73 +- 0.059, ROC-AUC 0.735 +- 0.076, F1-macro 0.683 (Table 1).

quantity_a: Accuracy of ANFIS on Kinect dual-task gait features, MCI vs HC, 150 Iranian older adults, protocol unstated
quantity_b: 10-fold CV accuracy of an RBF SVM on FreeSurfer structural-MRI morphometry, MCI vs HC, 207 Russian memory-clinic patients and volunteers
incompatible_if_same: Not as the rule reads incompatibility. Both are MCI-vs-HC accuracies, but they are two different methods on two different input representations, each reporting its own score; neither study claims that gait beats MRI or the reverse, so 93% and 73% do not refute each other.

gates.task: match: both binary MCI vs healthy controls (T1)
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: own IDAA Tehran cohort vs own Moscow memory-clinic cohort; no waiver on record
gates.validation_tier: uncertain: P-99 internal 10-fold CV; P-114 states no ANFIS evaluation protocol
gates.modality_family: mismatch: gait/motor (Kinect skeletal) vs structural MRI (FreeSurfer morphometry); no waiver on record

endpoint_and_metric: compatible in type (accuracy, MCI vs HC) but on different predictor sets and input representations in different cohorts
performance_validity: flag does not apply: P-99 reports 73% accuracy, not 99%; neither row is flagged and no contested value reaches 0.97.
independence: Independent: different groups, countries and cohorts; no shared authors.
grounds: The modality-family gate fails: P-114 classifies from Kinect gait parameters and P-99 from FreeSurfer structural-MRI morphometry, with no waiver on record.
The dataset-family gate fails: P-114's Tehran association cohort vs P-99's Moscow memory-clinic cohort (the same failure recorded for P-50 x P-99 in C-01).
The gap between 93% and 73% therefore confounds input representation, cohort and method, as in the C-80 precedent, and is not two results disagreeing about one measured quantity.
The resolution note's stated reason (P-99 'suspect accuracy >=97% (99.0%)') is false: P-99 reports 0.73 accuracy.

evidence_quotes.quote: the proposed ANFIS classifier had values of 93%, 90%, and 91.5% for accuracy, sensitivity, and F-score, respectively when all extracted gait parameters in the DTW condition for the classification of elderly subjects to MCI and HC groups.
Of 150 selected subjects, 80 subjects were healthy individuals without any cognitive impairments (HC subjects), and 70 subjects were elderly people with MCI.
The dataset for the study consists of 62 healthy volunteers and 145 patients with MCI obtained from the Memory Clinic (Moscow, Russia).
We propose a machine learning method, which achieved an accuracy of 73%
Due to an imbalanced dataset, for estimation of model performance, we used 10-fold cross-validation with the F1-metric.

record_defects: resolution_note says 'Paper B (P-99) reports suspect accuracy >=97% (99.0%)'; P-99 reports 73% accuracy (SVC 0.73 +- 0.059) and nothing near 99%.
The pack's P-114 PDF (paper_pdf_map.json, 'formula-unverified') is P-112's EEG paper, not the gait/ANFIS paper the record means.
dataset_equal='Yes' is wrong; validation_comparable='Yes' is unsupported (P-114 states no ANFIS protocol).

The 15 bridging papers named in the note (P-360, P-322, P-411, P-416, P-422, P-478, P-333, P-501, P-9, P-538, P-557, P-703, P-795, P-855, P-931) report scores in other modalities and contrasts; none shows a condition separating gait from sMRI accuracy, so partially_resolved_candidate is not supported. The P-795 entry is truncated prose.
what_would_change_the_verdict: A single study running gait and sMRI classifiers on one cohort, or a recorded waiver of the modality and dataset gates with a stated reason; neither exists here.
